newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs seen rangebound through Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs seen rangebound through Wednesday.

text.p: Belgian bonds were seen rangebound through Wednesday with many investors expected to wind up positions ahead of a two-day market holiday.

Bonds failed to get a lift from German jobless and U.S. manufacturing data on Tuesday and traders did not expect Wednesday's raft of U.S. numbers to encourage new position taking before Thursday and Friday, when the Belgian market is closed. "Over a long weekend when other markets are open anything can happen," one trader noted.
The 10-year OLO yield was at 5.87 percent late on Tuesday, up from 5.85 percent in early trade, but unchanged on the day.
The spread over Bunds was also little changed, oscillating between 10 and an unchanged 11 basis points.

Earlier figures from Germany's Federal Labour Office showed that German unemployment rose by 8,000 to a seasonally adjusted 4.299 million in April, when most players had expected a slight fall. Bunds initially firmed on the news but OLOs did nothing.

Bond positive U.S. data, which showed manufacturing orders fell in March, also failed to lift markets. Treasuries were lower mid-morning in the U.S., weighed down by the prospect of $17 billion supply of three-year notes.
